title: Pauper · mtg-kernel v2
summary: Eight Pauper decks with neutral protocol v2 choices. Every decision carries the seat's public event history (x_public_history_v1) and full Section 6.7 card knowledge. Entrants, GPT-6 Luna among them, face the frozen g115, a48 and c12 policies. Their checkpoint weights are unchanged; buffered choices use the versioned deterministic-completion-logprob/v1 selection adapter. Ratings use this panel only and cannot be compared numerically with the legacy Pauper or Standard boards. Private engine/checkpoints prevent independent game replay; public ledgers permit rating recomputation. The trusted child adapter is unsandboxed with self-reported isolation. Scores include local token-cap, timeout, provider HTTP503 and other transient provider-failure availability forfeits, with each kind reported separately, and malformed-choice forfeits, recorded as agent errors; they measure the deployed system including availability.

display.label: random
display.author: Spellbench
display.description: Picks uniformly at random among the offered actions. The anchor: its Elo is fixed at 1000.

display.label: Kernel 1
display.author: mipo
display.description: mtg-kernel policy network, Phase 1 lineage g block 115 (32,400 updates), sampled, no search. Trained on 6 of these 8 decks plus Terror; never saw Spy or CawGates. Neutral v2 choices, with deterministic-completion-logprob/v1 for buffered declarations and ordering; these ratings do not reuse the legacy v1 games.

display.label: Kernel 4
display.author: mipo
display.description: mtg-kernel policy network: the g115 lineage's r2 seed 1 continued by ordinary self-play RL to dose 512 (OH2, 82,944 updates), sampled, no search. The research program's best scoreboard checkpoint at the v2.3.0 boundary. Trained against a48 (20% of its opponents), so its a48 games are a training-opponent matchup.

display.label: GPT-6 Luna
display.author: OpenAI / mipo
display.description: gpt-6-luna through the authorized ChatGPT-plan provider, low reasoning, one-decision history, lean-v1 prompt with the last 8 public-history events, no card-text supplement. Forced choices bypass inference. Provider timeouts, other transient provider failures, the per-game token cap and malformed or unoffered choices forfeit the game; three forfeits in a row abort the run unrated. No request retries or fallback.

display.label: XMage MAD
display.author: XMage / Spellbench
display.description: XMage's ComputerPlayer7 (MAD) at skill 6 on one sampled hidden world, with the kit's synchronous 5000-node, 2000-option and 20000-operation budgets, permitted reconstruction, explicit horizons, dialog heuristics and fallback. Plays protocol v2 as an ordinary agent: each decision rebuilds an XMage world from the observation, public history and card knowledge, so it sees nothing the seat cannot.

display.label: XMage MAD four worlds
display.author: XMage / Spellbench
display.description: As kit-mad-1, voting over four sampled hidden worlds per decision. Plays protocol v2 as an ordinary agent: each decision rebuilds an XMage world from the observation, public history and card knowledge, so it sees nothing the seat cannot.

display.label: XMage MCTS, 8 iterations
display.author: XMage / Spellbench
display.description: XMage's MCTS on one sampled hidden world with knowledge-consistent rollouts: exactly 8 completed iterations per search (rollouts capped at 200 actions, truncated rollouts scored by the evaluator), never paced by the clock, so its play does not depend on machine speed or concurrency. MCTS combat keeps at most 128 engagements per expansion, in upstream's enumeration order. Replaces the bank-paced kit-mcts, whose searches stopped on the clock. Plays protocol v2 as an ordinary agent: each decision rebuilds an XMage world from the observation, public history and card knowledge, so it sees nothing the seat cannot.

display.label: gorge bot
display.author: gorge
display.description: gorge's default heuristic bot. On this engine it plays exactly as gorge's bot-auto-pay, which is therefore not entered. Plays protocol v2 as an ordinary agent through gorge's neutral world: each decision is rebuilt from the seat's own observation and candidates, with printed facts from gorge's frozen registry, so it sees nothing the seat cannot. Mana is paid by the engine. Affinity, Elves and Faeries each hold one card gorge cannot play fully.
